findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A reader can say what this is and why it matters after one paragraph.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The section meant to prove Athena's main promise is broken. Athena says it records models, verdict and cost, but the first section after the header shows only an error, and that is the first evidence a newcomer sees.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: What to do next is clear and easy to find. A link near the top jumps to Next steps, which lists prerequisites, the clone command, ./setup.sh and a first command to try.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: The page is titled after another project, and almost all of it is a dense study of firstmate. The study has twelve transition cards, a long glossary and 45 claims. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to read past a lot of material they did not ask for. The page never says plainly that skimming the study is enough.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>; sections "Transitions", "Glossary", "Claims and sources"

findings.text: A link in the header is aimed at the project owner, not a visitor. It is confusing on a public first page.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The study does show traceability: each statement links to a claim, and each claim links to exact lines at a pinned commit. This backs up the page's claim about what Athena can do.
findings.source: Next steps: "Check a statement: follow a bracketed claim id to the claim, then its source link to the file and lines in firstmate at the pinned commit."

findings.text: Some text in the study is internal jargon that a newcomer cannot decode, such as "recorded boundary" and "marked read".
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate, so no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."
